topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the module and sets out the key learning objectives for exploring the causes of cancer.

topics.label: Determinants of cancer development: genetics, environment, and chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises from the interplay of acquired mutations, inherited predisposition, environmental exposures, and chance, supported by epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms by which infectious agents promote malignancy, illustrating these principles through the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms through which physical radiation and metabolized chemical carcinogens cause DNA damage and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and two-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms in cancer development, including tumor promotion through chronic inflammation, stage-of-life host susceptibility, and the two-stage model.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogenicity and assess exposure risk.

topics.label: Conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarizing the central themes of environmental carcinogenesis and risk assessment.
